Summary: RECONX-E26 — Day 9: Kafka Topics, Producer & Event Payload
Description: Workshop 9 (part A). Declarative Kafka topics on boot, TradeEventProducer keyed by tradeRef for per-trade ordering, immutable TradeEvent record payload. Groups TICKET-ADV128 through ADV130.

Summary: RECONX-E27 — Day 9: Consumers — Recon, Audit & Alert
Description: Workshop 9 (part B). Three @KafkaListener consumers in three distinct consumer groups (recon-service, audit-service, alert-service) for fan-out with independent SLAs. Groups TICKET-ADV131 through ADV133.

Summary: RECONX-E28 — Day 9: DLQ, Retry, Replay & Event Sourcing
Description: Workshop 9 (part C). DefaultErrorHandler with exponential backoff retries, dead-letter publishing to trade-events-dlq, DLQ consumer plus admin replay endpoint, and event-sourced trade state rebuild from audit_log. Groups TICKET-ADV134 through ADV138.

Summary: RECONX-E29 — Day 9: Metrics, Grafana, Integration Tests & AI Review
Description: Workshop 9 (part D). Kafka metrics via Micrometer/Prometheus, Grafana panels for lag, throughput and DLQ count with alerting, Testcontainers integration tests for happy path and DLQ routing, and an AI-assisted consumer config review. Groups TICKET-ADV139 through ADV145.

Summary: TICKET-ADV128 — Kafka topics: trade-events, recon-results, system-alerts + DLQ
Description: GOAL: declare the three primary Kafka topics plus the trade-events DLQ topic so the broker creates them automatically on application startup. DONE WHEN: a @Configuration class declares four NewTopic beans — trade-events (3 partitions), trade-events-dlq (3 partitions), recon-results (2 partitions), system-alerts (1 partition), each with replicas(1). After backend restart Kafdrop shows all four topics with correct partition counts with no manual kafka-topics.sh run, and topic names are exposed as public static final String constants on the config class.

Summary: TICKET-ADV129 — TradeEventProducer keyed by tradeRef
Description: GOAL: build a producer component that publishes TradeEvent messages to the trade-events topic, keyed by tradeRef so all events for the same trade preserve order on one partition. DONE WHEN: a @Component TradeEventProducer exposes publish(TradeEvent event) sending to trade-events with message key event.tradeRef(); the send is asynchronous with failures logged via the future's whenComplete callback (no blocking .get()); after invoking publish, Kafdrop shows the message under trade-events with the expected partition assignment.

Summary: TICKET-ADV130 — TradeEvent payload record
Description: GOAL: define the immutable Kafka event payload as a Java record carrying event metadata and a before/after trade snapshot. DONE WHEN: a TradeEvent record in the dto package has eventId (UUID), tradeRef, eventType, timestamp (Instant), before and after snapshots; a nested EventType enum has TRADE_CREATED, TRADE_UPDATED, TRADE_CANCELLED; three static factories created/updated/cancelled each generate a fresh UUID and Instant.now(); Jackson round-trip (publish then consume) preserves all fields including the snapshots.

Summary: TICKET-ADV131 — ReconciliationConsumer (recon-service group)
Description: GOAL: wire a consumer on the trade-events topic that triggers reconciliation logic for every event, in the recon-service consumer group. DONE WHEN: a @Component ReconciliationConsumer has a @KafkaListener(topics = trade-events, groupId = recon-service) method receiving a TradeEvent; it dispatches on eventType — TRADE_CREATED/TRADE_UPDATED call reconEngine.scheduleRecon(tradeRef), TRADE_CANCELLED calls cancelPendingRecon(tradeRef); after boot Kafdrop shows the recon-service group assigned across all three trade-events partitions; publishing one event triggers exactly one recon dispatch.

Summary: TICKET-ADV132 — AuditEventConsumer persists events to audit_log
Description: GOAL: persist every TradeEvent to the audit_log table using a separate consumer group, so the event log becomes the foundation of the event-sourcing rebuild. DONE WHEN: a @Component AuditEventConsumer has a @KafkaListener(topics = trade-events, groupId = audit-service) method annotated @Transactional; it builds an AuditLogEntry from the event (eventId, tradeRef, operation = eventType.name(), before/after data, occurredAt = event timestamp) and saves via AuditLogRepository; after publishing 10 events for one trade, audit_log contains exactly 10 rows for that trade in event-time order.

Summary: TICKET-ADV133 — AlertConsumer on system-alerts
Description: GOAL: listen on the system-alerts topic and surface every alert at WARN level, with a pluggable sink for Slack or another notifier. DONE WHEN: a @Component AlertConsumer has a @KafkaListener(topics = system-alerts, groupId = alert-service) method receiving a SystemAlert DTO; each alert is logged at WARN with severity, code and message; the consumer calls a constructor-injected AlertSink.notify(alert) (starter NoopAlertSink left in place); Kafdrop shows consumer group alert-service registered on the single system-alerts partition.

Summary: TICKET-ADV134 — Dead-Letter Queue wiring (DefaultErrorHandler + recoverer)
Description: GOAL: configure a DefaultErrorHandler that publishes records to a *-dlq topic on the same partition number after retries are exhausted. DONE WHEN: a @Configuration class declares a DefaultErrorHandler bean built from a DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer; the destination resolver maps each failed record to a TopicPartition named record.topic() + -dlq with the same record.partition(); the trade-events listener container factory is wired to this handler; deserialization exceptions are added to the not-retryable list so poison pills go straight to DLQ without retries.

Summary: TICKET-ADV135 — Retry strategy with exponential backoff
Description: GOAL: tune the error handler's backoff so retries follow an exponential schedule (roughly 1s, 2s, 4s) and stop after about three attempts before the message lands in the DLQ. DONE WHEN: the ExponentialBackOff is constructed with initial interval 1000 ms and multiplier 2.0; setMaxElapsedTime caps total retry wait at roughly 8 seconds yielding three retries before DLQ publish; a test that throws on every retry shows three retry attempts in the logs, then a DLQ publish, then the offset commits with no infinite loop; you can state in one sentence why fixed backoff is the wrong choice here.

Summary: TICKET-ADV136 — DLQ consumer and admin replay endpoint
Description: GOAL: build a consumer on trade-events-dlq that records each failed message, plus an admin REST endpoint that re-publishes a single DLQ message back to the main topic. DONE WHEN: a @Component DlqConsumer listens on trade-events-dlq (groupId dlq-monitor), receives the ConsumerRecord plus the exception-message header, persists a DlqMessage row (eventId, tradeRef, originalTopic, partition, offset, payload, reason, firstSeen) and logs at ERROR; POST /api/v1/admin/dlq/replay accepts required eventId and dryRun (default false) — dry-run returns what would be replayed, real run re-publishes via TradeEventProducer and deletes the DLQ row; the endpoint is protected with @PreAuthorize hasRole ADMIN.

Summary: TICKET-ADV137 — Event sourcing rebuild (TradeAggregator)
Description: GOAL: build a TradeAggregator service whose rebuild(tradeRef) method reads every event for that trade from audit_log, ordered by timestamp, and folds them into current state. DONE WHEN: a @Service TradeAggregator exposes Optional<JsonNode> rebuild(String tradeRef); it reads AuditLogEntry rows via findByTradeRefOrderByOccurredAtAsc; TRADE_CREATED and TRADE_UPDATED set the running state to the entry's afterData while TRADE_CANCELLED sets it to null; the method returns Optional.empty() when there are no events and Optional.ofNullable(state) otherwise, so a cancelled trade yields an empty Optional.

Summary: TICKET-ADV138 — Admin audit endpoint for trade event history
Description: GOAL: expose GET /api/v1/audit/trades/{tradeRef}/events so admins and recon analysts can fetch the full event history for any trade, oldest first. DONE WHEN: a @RestController at /api/v1/audit/trades has a @GetMapping /{tradeRef}/events method returning List<TradeEvent>; it is protected with @PreAuthorize hasAnyRole ADMIN, RECON_ANALYST; the response is ordered by event timestamp ascending and includes every event with no pagination; unauthenticated requests return 401 and authenticated users without either role return 403.

Summary: TICKET-ADV139 — Kafka metrics via Micrometer
Description: GOAL: expose Kafka client metrics on the Prometheus actuator endpoint so Grafana can scrape them. DONE WHEN: application.yml enables management.metrics.binders.kafka.enabled true; the consumer config sets metric.reporters to KafkaClientMetrics under spring.kafka.consumer.properties; management.endpoints.web.exposure.include contains prometheus; curling /actuator/prometheus and grepping kafka_consumer returns at least kafka_consumer_records_lag, kafka_consumer_records_consumed_total and kafka_consumer_fetch_total with non-null values after publishing a few events.

Summary: TICKET-ADV140 — Grafana panel: consumer lag by topic
Description: GOAL: add a Time Series panel to Grafana showing consumer lag aggregated per topic, with red/yellow thresholds. DONE WHEN: a panel titled Consumer lag by topic exists in the Kafka dashboard row; the query is sum by (topic) (kafka_consumer_records_lag); thresholds are yellow at 100 and red at 1000; after publishing 100 messages and pausing a consumer for 30 seconds the panel visibly shows lag growth for the affected topic.

Summary: TICKET-ADV141 — Grafana panel: messages/sec produced vs consumed
Description: GOAL: add a Time Series panel that overlays produce rate and consume rate so a slow consumer is visible at a glance. DONE WHEN: a panel titled Throughput: produced vs consumed shows two series labelled consumed and produced; the consumed query is sum(rate(kafka_consumer_records_consumed_total[1m])) and the produced query is sum(rate(kafka_producer_record_send_total[1m])); during steady state the two lines track each other closely and deliberately throttling a consumer makes them diverge visibly.

Summary: TICKET-ADV142 — Grafana panel: DLQ count and alert
Description: GOAL: add a Stat panel showing total messages routed to the trade-events DLQ, plus an alerting rule that fires on any DLQ activity. DONE WHEN: a Stat panel titled DLQ message count shows sum(kafka_consumer_records_consumed_total{topic=trade-events-dlq}); an alerting rule named KafkaDlqMessages fires when that expression is greater than 0 for one minute with severity critical; the alert annotation includes a summary and a description pointing operators to /api/v1/admin/dlq; deliberately failing a consumer fires the alert in Grafana within about 90 seconds.

Summary: TICKET-ADV143 — Integration test: end-to-end happy path (Testcontainers)
Description: GOAL: write a @SpringBootTest that boots Testcontainers Kafka, publishes 100 events, and waits until 100 audit rows are persisted using Awaitility instead of Thread.sleep. DONE WHEN: a KafkaPipelineIT test class is annotated @SpringBootTest and @Testcontainers; a static @Container KafkaContainer uses confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.6.0; a @DynamicPropertySource method registers spring.kafka.bootstrap-servers from the container; the test publishes 100 TradeEvent.created events with distinct trade refs and asserts via Awaitility that auditRepo.count() increases by 100 within 30 seconds, passing consistently via ./mvnw -Dtest=KafkaPipelineIT verify.

Summary: TICKET-ADV144 — Integration test: DLQ routing on consumer failure
Description: GOAL: write a Testcontainers test proving a failing listener causes the message to land on trade-events-dlq after retries are exhausted. DONE WHEN: a DlqRoutingIT test class boots Testcontainers Kafka the same way as KafkaPipelineIT; it uses @MockBean ReconciliationEngine with Mockito.doThrow so every recon dispatch fails; it publishes one TradeEvent.created with tradeRef TRD-DLQ-1 and asserts via Awaitility that a raw Kafka consumer subscribed to trade-events-dlq sees a record with that tradeRef within 30 seconds; the raw consumer sets JsonDeserializer.TRUSTED_PACKAGES to * so it can deserialise the DLQ payload.

Summary: TICKET-ADV145 — AI-assisted Kafka consumer config review
Description: GOAL: use Claude to review the Kafka consumer configuration for production readiness, then file a PR recording each finding with an explicit accept/reject/defer decision. DONE WHEN: the Kafka section of application.yml and KafkaErrorHandlerConfig.java are pasted into Claude with a focused review prompt covering backpressure/poll tuning, error handling and retry/DLQ, idempotence, observability, and security; the prompt tells Claude to list findings only (no whole-file rewrite) with config key, recommended value, and one-line justification each; a PR description lists every finding with a team decision column (accept/reject/defer) and one-line rationale; at least one finding is accepted, one rejected, and one deferred with reasons stated.
